![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/3da35964a3877c7a0b3fce7e4f8c2db2d320f1d69f720541afa5dd1428447b73.png)

Find the area $A$ of the shaded region that lies between the polar curves $r=2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ and $r=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the values of $\theta $ for which the two curves intersect:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =2 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two solutions for $\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ]:$

$$
\theta =\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{5\pi }{6}
$$

To determine which is the inner function and which is the outer, let's draw an arrow from the origin that passes through the shaded region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/dd265c911aa4fc5713b0e53cea2ee751e84cd7c54b2b2aefb83bfae8d1f7d92f.png)

The arrow

- *enters* the region through the inner function $r=2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $r=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

To find the area, we use the formula

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where

$\,$ ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{\pi }{6},\,$ and $\,{\theta }_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{6}.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{5\pi /6}((2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}-(2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{5\pi /6}(4{sin}^{2}⁡\theta -(4-8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{5\pi /6}(8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -4)\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-8\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -4\theta )\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{5\pi /6} \\  & =-2(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\theta )\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{5\pi /6} \\  & =-2(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6})+\frac{5\pi }{6})+2(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})+\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-2(-\sqrt{3}+\frac{5\pi }{6})+2(\sqrt{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =4\sqrt{3}-\frac{4\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
